Wirtschaftlichkeitslücke, d.h. in Höhe der Differenz zwischen dem Barwert aller Einnahmen und dem Barwert der Ausgaben für den Netzaufbau und -betrieb, erfolgen. title: Netherlands – Data-processing services – The procurement and processing of satellite data for the Netherlands Satellite Data Portal
description: Since 2012, the Netherlands Space Office has been purchasing satellite data on behalf of the Dutch government and making these data available free of charge to Dutch entities via the Satellite Data Portal (http://www.satellietdataportaal.nl, ftp.satellietdataportaal.nl, and api.satellietdataportaal.nl). The current contracts for the purchase and processing of the data will expire on February 1, 2026. For the continuation of the satellite data portal, raw satellite data and processed data products derived from these raw data will be purchased for a new period of three years (from February 1, 2026, to February 1, 2029), with the option to extend the contract three times by one year until February 1, 2032 at the latest. The work within this contract includes the acquisition and delivery of raw VHR optical satellite data and the processing of these satellite data into usable products, which will be made available via the Satellite Data Portal. The Contracting Authority intends to conclude a Contract with one Contractor for a period of 3 years, running from 1 February 2026 to 1 February 2029, including a unilateral option for the Contracting Authority to extend the contract three times by one year until February 1, 2032 at the latest. The Tendering Authority has a total contract value (including all three optional extension years) of EUR 7,000,000 excluding Netherlands VAT and (if applicable) including local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees. The maximum total contract value for the initial three year contract period is EUR 3,500,000 excluding Netherlands VAT and (if applicable) including local foreign VAT and all other costs and/or fees.

title: Support services to Simpl’s Programme - Support Office (PSO II) Open procedure
description:
This is the renewal of the first Simpl PSO Framework contract, which was awarded in 2023 following the publication of calls for tenders CNECT/2023/OP/0050: https://etendering.ted.europa.eu/cft/cft-display.html?cftId=14888 .
The objective of PSOII call for tenders is to procure services to support and improve Simpl programme quality management system built to ensure a high and stable quality level of the IT products related to Simpl programme. 
It is also meant to strengthen the project management support and horizontal coordination tasks across the involved stakeholders, boosting efficient processes inspired by open-source best practices while complying to European Commission procurement rules. 
The PSO II framework contract will follow up on the existing PSO framework contract after it ends of delivery of the third specific contract (September 2026).

title: Ireland – Vans – OPERATIONAL LEASE OF ONE WHEELCHAIR-ACCESSIBLE VAN AND ONE CAR
description: Depaul Ireland invites suitably qualified and experienced vehicle leasing providers to submit tenders for the operational lease of one wheelchair-accessible van (Lot 1) and one car (Lot 2) for a period of 36 months, with full maintenance included. Depaul Ireland is a charity working with individuals and families experiencing homelessness and those at risk of homelessness. Its services include emergency accommodation, supported housing, Housing First, health and wellbeing services, community-based support and administrative functions. Many services operate continuously and support vulnerable individuals, so vehicle reliability, accessibility, safety and continuity of service are essential. The vehicle is intended primarily to support Depaul Ireland's Housing First and related operational activities, including the safe transport of service users, including wheelchair users, and staff. The successful Tenderer will be expected to work collaboratively with Depaul Ireland's nominated Contract Manager and relevant service personnel throughout the lease period.

title: TRANSMIT AND RECEIVE DUAL POLARIZATIONACTIVE ANTENNA BASED ON SCALABLE TILE ASSEMBLYFOR GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITES (ARTES AT 5B.248) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a scalable Ku- or Ka-band tile assembly enabling compact combined transmit and receive active antenna for satellites in geosynchronous orbit. This will include the development of a mechanical and thermal concept. Targeted Improvements: Reduction of the number of antennas at spacecraft level by a factor of 2. Description: There is a trend for telecommunication satellites in Geostationary Orbits to reduce the size of the platform whilst maintainingcapacity of the system. The accommodation of several active antennas in such reduced size platforms is becoming more challenging and the need for integrated transmit and receive phased array antennas is growing. The current feed chain solutions are often based onhollow or ridge waveguide technology which meet performance requirements but result in bulky implementations and therefore they arenot compatible for implementing transmit and receive in the same aperture while keeping both orthogonal polarisations. New ways of implementing RF components based on planar technologies have been previously studied but this technology is trading in insertion loss and RF bandwidth performance. New PCB based technology such as Air-Filled Surface Integrated Waveguide (AFSIW), gap-technology andadvanced manufacturing techniques have the potential to significantly reduce the volume with respect to the current state of the art, whilst maintaining good RF performance. Metamaterials, which are engineered materials with unique properties, are also a potential solution to reduce the volume of feed chain assemblies. This activity will develop in a concept of a dual polarised combined transmit and receive active antenna in Ku- or Ka-band. Trade-off studies of several antenna topology designs will be performed. Breadboarding of critical components of the feed chain will be carried out including the development of a low loss filtering solution. A breadboard of a tile assembly will be developed and tested. For the breadboard tile assembly off-the shelf high power amplifiers and lownoise amplifiers shall be baselined. Thermal and mechanical assessment and experimental tests of the tile-assembly will be carried to evaluate the performance of the developed active antenna.
